sources.entry: One Time Secret - Share sensitive information securely with self-destructing links that are only viewable once. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Docker/Ruby/Nodejs

summary.one_liner: Onetime Secret is a self-hostable web app for sharing sensitive information through single-use links that self-destruct after being viewed once.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a one-time secret as a single-use URL, so passwords and other sensitive text can be sent over email or chat without leaving lasting copies. Links are destroyed after they are viewed. The project runs as a Docker image that depends on Redis, configured via environment variables such as REDIS_URL, SECRET, HOST and SSL. An admin ("colonel") account can be created from the command line with bin/ots. The README points to further material for reverse proxy setup, a full authentication stack (PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, MFA, WebAuthn), Docker Compose stacks, configuration reference, and contributing guidelines. A live demo is hosted at OnetimeSecret.com.
use_cases: share a password without leaving it in chat logs
send one-time links containing sensitive text
run a team-internal self-destructing message tool
how_to_run: docker run -p 3000:3000 -d --name onetimesecret --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway -e REDIS_URL=redis://host.docker.internal:6379/0 -e SECRET="$(cat .ots_secret)" -e HOST=localhost:3000 -e SSL=false onetimesecret/onetimesecret:v0.26.14
docker exec onetimesecret bin/ots customers create me@example.com --role colonel
notable: Links are single-use and self-destruct after the first view
Docker image with Redis backend and environment-variable configuration
Optional full authentication stack with MFA and WebAuthn
Admin account creation via bin/ots command line
Docker Compose options for simple and full deployments
caveats: Losing the SECRET key makes existing secrets unreadable and is not recoverable
The quick start uses SSL=false; production use needs SSL and hardening per the self-hosting guide
Full authentication requires additional services (PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ)
